name: Change.org
description: Change.org is a nonprofit-owned petition platform where people create campaigns, gather signatures, publish updates and advocate around social and political issues.
agentUseSummary: Change.org cannot currently be installed as a Relay connector because its retired public v1 API no longer has official documentation, key registration, support or a published replacement contract. Relay will not revive decade-old endpoints, scrape public petitions, collect account credentials or automate private campaign-management workflows.

blocked.label: Connect Change.org
blocked.description: Change.org publishes no current customer-authorized authentication or API contract for third-party account integrations.

blocked.label: Use the retired Change.org v1 API
blocked.description: Relay does not depend on retired, unsupported petition endpoints or historical API key and request-signature schemes.

blocked.label: Scrape Change.org petitions
blocked.description: Relay does not crawl petition pages or reconstruct private APIs from first-party application traffic.

blocked.label: Automate Change.org campaign management
blocked.description: Relay does not collect Change.org passwords, sign petitions, create campaigns or automate private campaign dashboards.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No action is exposed until Change.org publishes and supports a current customer-authorized developer contract.

runtimeSupport.description: No current supported Change.org API contract exists to mount as OpenClaw tools.
No current supported Change.org API contract exists to mount as Hermes tools.

providerSetup.blocker: Change.org's former v1 developer documentation, API-key registration surface and official API documentation repository are no longer published. The current Help Center describes only first-party petition and signature-download workflows, while current terms reserve Change.org's API without granting or documenting a third-party customer contract. The retired surface handled petition signers and politically sensitive data and cannot be treated as supported merely because historical endpoints may sometimes respond.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request credentials or expose Connect. Reconsider only after Change.org publishes current official authentication, endpoint, permission, rate-limit, lifecycle and data-processing documentation and confirms customer-authorized third-party use; then complete legal/security review and Railway-staging acceptance with representative authorized data.

evidence.supports: Change.org's current 2026 Help Center describes the active first-party petition platform and campaign-owner controls but publishes no developer API entry point or authentication contract.
Current petition-management documentation routes starters through the product UI for edits, updates, signature downloads, deletion and signature controls rather than a supported API.
Current terms reserve Change.org's APIs, databases and services as platform property but do not publish a customer-callable integration contract or authorize resurrection of the retired v1 surface.

The May 2026 privacy policy identifies contact data, precise campaign activity, political opinions, voter-registration data, location, petition signatures and other sensitive records, making unsupported access unacceptable.
The current product remains active as a first-party petition and campaign platform, so this is an API-support classification rather than a retired-product classification.
